Minigraf: The Bitemporal Graph Database Incorporated for AI and Web

The video features Minigraf, a built-in, single file database written in Rust, with queries in Datalog and bitemporal model. Explains the difference between transaction time and valid time, uses on AI agents, mobile apps and browser, and project boundaries.

A graph bank that remembers the past

The video starts from a question: What if a local database could remember all the past states, without too much extra storage and without a server? Usually, by overwriting a given, the history gets lost, and maintaining complete audit in the local environment is difficult 00:20.

Project documentation defines Minigraf as "o SQLite of bitemporal graph databases": a single, built-in and unconfigured file, such as SQLite, but for connected data and full history 01:05.

What is Minigraf

Minigraf is written in Rust and works from a single file with extension .graph. A line of code opens the file and the bank is ready 01:48.

He keeps the facts as edges of a graph, accepts queries in Datalog and maintains all information history 02:08.

According to the video, there are mature graph banks, such as Neo4j and XTDB (which also has temporal resources), and SQLite dominates embedded storage. Minigraf would be the only native Rust solution that combines Datalog, single file, bitemporal features and web browser execution by WebAssembly 02:30.

Why Datalog and not SQL

SQL was designed for tables; Datalog, for logical relationships and, therefore, for graphs 02:51.

Searching "amigos from friends of friends" is natural in Datalog, which is recursive by design, without the various joins that weigh on SQL. The model is entity-attribute-value: a fact in the bank is an edge 03:12.

Grammar is compact and uniform, and the entire Minigraf language fits into the system prompt of an AI wizard. With few examples, a language model generates correct queries 03:33.

Two times: transaction and validity

The Datomic-inspired bitemporal model uses two timelines 04:16:

  • Transaction time: the moment the system recorded the information 04:16.
  • Valid time: when that happened in the real world 04:16.

With both, you can correct the past without erasing the record of when the system learned of the correction 04:37.

The video example 04:37:

1. In minute 1, the app is offline and records a wrong value 04:37. 2. In minute 5, the connection returns and a retroactive correction arrives: in minute 1, the right value was another 04:37. 3. In minute 10, you can ask the bank what the system knew in minute 2, before correction, and the Minigraf reconstructs that view. 04:58.

Use cases

Video cites three fronts: memory of AI agents, local storage in mobile applications and browser applications 05:19.

  • AI agents. The agent keeps what he believes is true to decide. If wrong, the correction does not delete the error record. In a GraphRAG pattern, the vector bank searches for similarity, and the Minigraf shows the relationships and what the agent knew at the time of the decision 05:40.
  • Mobile apps. Offline-first storage: in a health application used in the field, data is recorded without connection, and an old typing error is fixed with a retroactive fact without losing audit 06:01. With UniFFI-generated libraries, you can use the Kotlin bank on Android or Swift on iOS without writing Rust 06:22.
  • Navigator. Compiled for WebAssembly, Minigraf runs in the browser and records the data in IndexedDB. There is a web playground with a timeline that shows the graph changing, and experimental support to WASI and edge computing 06:42.

Scope and limits

The Minigraf is a library that runs along with the application. Not a distributed database: no network protocol, clustering or automatic replication 07:05.

Also does not follow the client-server model: each instance owns the file itself. And it does not replace a time series bank of sensor metrics; the focus is to track knowledge over time 07:27.

In banks recorded in file, each serialized fact has a maximum of 4,080 bytes; the memory version does not have this limit 07:49. Large texts go to the file system, and the graph saves only context 08:09.

The project targets less than 1 million nodes: it is optimized for smaller scenarios, with fast reading and little memory use, such as SQLite 08:09.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Minigraf replace a server database?

Nope. It is embedded in the application, is not distributed and does not follow the client-server model 07:05.

What is a bitemporal bank?

It is a bank that records two times for each fact: when the system recorded the information and when it was worth it in the real world 04:16.

About the video

In this explanatory video, know the **Minigraf**, an embedded graph memory solution (*embedded*) developed for AI agents, mobile applications and browsers**.

The Minigraf links the practicality of a lightweight database in a single file in `.graph' format to the power of native queries in **Datalog** and the **bitemporal** model. With the ability to make time travel (*time travel*), Minigraf tracks both transaction time and information validity time, allowing you to audit AI agent decisions and reconstruct past data states without losing the history of changes.

---

** Main highlights of the Minigraf:**
- **Sees in Datalog:** native crossing of graphs and recursive rules in a simple way.
- ** Bitemporal support: ** Complete *time travel* support using transaction time and expiration time.
- **Incorporated Bank and Zero Configuration:** run from a single file `.graph`.
- **Advanced resources:** includes *window functions* and *prepared states*.
- **Multiplatform:**Native support for Rust, Python, iOS, Android and browsers via WebAssembly (WASM).
